key_insight: K2/Rb2SnGeX6 lead-free double perovskites are predicted by DFT to be stable, ductile, and highly tunable semiconductors with direct bandgaps spanning 1.44 to 0.64 eV.
engineering_relevance: These materials could support safer photovoltaic absorbers, tandem solar layers, and high-performance thermoelectric devices without using toxic lead.
method: DFT study of the K/Rb and Cl/Br/I double-perovskite series
Calculated formation energy, tolerance factor, and octahedral factor for stability
Evaluated elastic, electronic, optical, and thermoelectric properties
evidence_signal: The abstract reports six stable cubic compounds, direct bandgaps that decrease with heavier halogens, and a peak predicted thermoelectric performance of ZT = 2.4 for K2SnGeI6 at 1000 K.
watch_item: The results are computational predictions only, so experimental synthesis, phase stability, and defect sensitivity still need validation.
paper_title: First-Principles Study of Novel Lead-Free Double Perovskite \b{eta}2SnGeX6 (\b{eta} = K, Rb; X = Cl, Br, I) for thermomechanical, optoelectronic and outstanding thermoelectric applications
